strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical value: addresses genuine MLLM limitations in deepfake detection reasoning (hallucinations, inconsistency, poor visual grounding)
Strong experimental results: 89.91% F1 achieves 14% improvement over SIDA baseline; 4.55/5.0 reasoning score exceeds Gemini-2.5; comprehensive cross-domain evaluation
Thoughtful dataset pipeline: three-step DF-R5 generation (feature discovery → scoring → reasoning) designed to reduce bias and hallucinations, with 115k image-reasoning pairs
Comprehensive ablation studies: demonstrates necessity of both VCR and PCR rewards, outperforms PPO/GRPO on transfer tasks, multiple evaluation angles
Reproducibility: detailed implementation details (hyperparameters, algorithms, prompts), promise to release code and dataset
Effective presentation: Figure 1 clearly illustrates MLLM limitations and PRPO improvements; generally well-written
weaknesses: Critical evaluation methodology concern: reasoning quality (Table 6) evaluated exclusively by GPT-4o without human verification; potential circularity and bias in assessing MLLM outputs using another LLM

Crude reward design lacks principled justification: PCR uses simple hard-coded dictionary matching (predefined fake/real/negation terms) that is brittle and task-specific; VCR uses lossy YAKE keyword extraction instead of learned similarity

Incomplete analysis of Gemini dependency: dataset entirely distilled from Gemini-2.5 (Steps 2-3), yet DX-LLaVA underperforms Gemini (84.64% vs 85.00%); generalization from single-source distillation is unclear; fair comparison with Gemini not established

Limited algorithmic novelty: DX-LLaVA simply replaces ViT with ConvNeXT (incremental); PRPO adapts GRPO from token-level to paragraph-level (straightforward adaptation); primary contribution is engineering application rather than novel algorithms
Misleading test-time RL framing: paper claims PRPO 'can be applied at test time' but experiments (Tables 4, 8) show application during training on unseen domains, not true inference-time adaptation

Generalization scope limitations: all experiments on face-based deepfakes within single dataset family (DF40 variants); no evaluation on non-facial deepfakes, video deepfakes, or completely different generation methods
Incomplete ablations: no hyperparameter M sensitivity analysis; Table 7 reward ablation only on SD domain (how do contributions vary across domains?); no qualitative error analysis or failure cases
Statistical rigor gaps: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; single runs reported without repeated experiments; high cross-domain variance (Table 4) without statistical summary

Dataset quality concerns: 115k images filtered with Gemini but no human verification of reasoning annotations; no inter-annotator agreement metrics; Gemini-based filtering creates evaluation circularity
Missing computational analysis: training requires 8 H200 GPUs; no inference-time cost analysis despite YAKE extraction and CLIP similarity computation during deployment

strengths: Addresses an important problem combining deepfake detection accuracy with explainability, which is practically significant
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including cross-domain testing, ablation studies, and multi-criteria explanation quality assessment
Valuable dataset contribution (DF-R5 with 115k reasoning annotations across 5 generative models) that fills a gap in deepfake detection research
Test-time application of PRPO is flexible and doesn't require retraining with annotated data
Consistent improvements across domains with detailed ablations showing the importance of both VCR and PCR components
weaknesses: Fundamental circular dependency: training data is distilled FROM Gemini-2.5, then the model is fine-tuned on Gemini annotations. This severely limits novelty claims and makes the 2% improvement over Gemini (78.08% vs 85%) unsurprising rather than impressive

Reward functions rely on heuristic design without rigorous validation: PCR uses predefined term dictionaries that are neither fully disclosed nor validated against ground truth; VCR uses YAKE keyword extraction which is crude and unvalidated for this task
Critical reproducibility gaps: full dictionary for PCR not provided, dataset URL missing, hyperparameter choices (α=10.0, β=0.01) lack justification or sensitivity analysis
Evaluation entirely depends on GPT-4o for explanation quality (Table 6) with no human evaluation; GPT-4o may simply prefer longer, structured outputs by design rather than truly assessing grounding
No statistical significance testing reported; all improvements presented as point estimates without confidence intervals or p-values, making 1-2% gains potentially within noise

Methodological novelty is limited: PRPO is a straightforward modification of GRPO (paragraph-level vs token-level advantages), and DX-LLaVA's ConvNeXT encoder substitution is an incremental architectural change

Alarming inter-domain generalization: Table 2 shows 99.57% intra-domain accuracy drops to 59.40% inter-domain; high variance across domains (SiT 71.26% vs StyleGAN3 99.32%) is unexplained, yet paper emphasizes average 89.91%
Computational cost and efficiency not discussed: test-time RL requires sampling multiple outputs, but sample sensitivity, inference overhead, and wall-clock time are not reported
Dataset scope is limited: all images from single source (DF-40), only 5 generative models covered; as generative models evolve rapidly, this dataset risks becoming quickly outdated

strengths: Addresses important problem of explainable deepfake detection with clear motivation and practical relevance
Valuable dataset contribution: DF-R5 with 115k images and reasoning annotations; clever three-step pipeline reduces hallucination
Strong experimental results: 89.91% F1 (14% improvement over SIDA); explanation quality 4.55/5 exceeds Gemini-2.5 (4.2/5)
Well-motivated technical approach: paragraph-level RL optimization addresses reasoning quality; VCR+PCR rewards sensibly handle visual consistency and prediction alignment
Comprehensive evaluation: multiple metrics (detection accuracy, explanation quality), proper inter-domain protocol, thoughtful ablations showing both rewards are necessary
Solid architecture design: ConvNeXT over ViT well-justified for local artifact detection; proper comparison with other RL methods (PPO, GRPO)
Good reproducibility: detailed implementation, hyperparameters, prompts provided; code/dataset promised for release
weaknesses: Dataset quality concerns: reasoning annotations entirely from Gemini (77.6% accuracy); no human validation or inter-annotator agreement; Gemini distillation introduces systematic biases

Reward functions oversimplified: VCR uses crude YAKE + cosine similarity (no validation that extracted keywords drive predictions); PCR uses predefined dictionaries (brittle, limited expressiveness); averaging weights (Eq. 4) appear arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis
Limited technical novelty: PRPO is essentially GRPO applied at paragraph level; main contribution is reward design rather than algorithmic innovation—incremental modification of existing approach

Generalization concerns: significant variance across domains (SiT: 71.26% vs ~95% others); inter-domain drop (70.4% F1) suggests unresolved domain shift; only evaluated on facial deepfakes; no error analysis or discussion of failure modes
Automatic evaluation bias: explanation quality assessed by GPT-4o, not humans; no inter-rater reliability or human study; risk of optimizing toward GPT-4o's preferences rather than true faithfulness

Missing experimental details: number of inference samples L unspecified; PPO clipping parameter ε sensitivity not analyzed; computational cost of test-time RL not discussed; large unexplained gap in Table 5 (DX-LLaVA vs Gemini-2.5 vs PRPO)
Limited baseline comparisons: missing recent explainable detection methods (FakeBench, FFAA); no comparison with other explanation alignment techniques from vision-language literature
Incomplete reproducibility: code/dataset location listed but URL not provided; some inference/sampling strategies during PRPO not fully specified; feature term dictionaries incomplete
Ethical discussion limited: no analysis of adversarial robustness to fool explanations; potential false confidence in unreliable explanations not addressed

strengths: Comprehensive multi-faceted contribution combining dataset (DF-R5 with 115k reasoning-annotated images), architecture (DX-LLaVA with ConvNeXT), and algorithm (PRPO). Each component is well-motivated.

Rigorous experimental validation with strong cross-domain evaluation (inter-domain setup), thorough ablation studies (Tables 7-11), human validation (Table 16), and analysis showing minimal Gemini-reasoning overlap (2.35% 4-gram, Table 13).

Well-justified ConvNeXT architectural choice with multi-faceted evidence: saliency visualization (Figure 10), feature space analysis (Figures 11-12), and substantial ablation gains (+24.10% F1 inter-domain).

Significant empirical improvements: +11.83% average F1 on unseen domains (78.08% → 89.91%), reasoning quality exceeds Gemini-2.5 (4.55 vs 4.2/5.0), particularly strong on challenging SiT domain (+44.73%).

Exceptional reproducibility: detailed implementation specs (Table 15), full prompts (Appendix A.2), hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Tables 18-19), computational profiling (Tables 20-21), and comprehensive qualitative examples with failure analysis.

Honest and thoughtful treatment of limitations: acknowledges domain focus (face-centric), identifies specific failure modes (sparse-artifact problem in SiT), and discusses ethical considerations in impact statement.
weaknesses: Heuristic reward design lacks principled justification: VCR uses arbitrary YAKE+CLIP similarity normalization without justifying superiority over alternatives; PCR uses brittle dictionary-based term matching rather than learned representations. Table 7 shows PCR alone achieves only 70.98% F1.

Counterintuitive finding inadequately explained: Unsupervised PRPO (95.88% F1) dramatically outperforms supervised PRPO (78.75%, Table 11). The explanation that label-free rewards enhance domain invariance is speculative and deserves deeper investigation. Does this undermine the visual grounding assumption?

Orthogonal component design: ConvNeXT improvement alone achieves +33.2% accuracy (Table 9), nearly matching PRPO's +3.2% gain on DX-LLaVA. Components feel weakly connected; clearer narrative needed on why this specific combination is necessary.

Persistent domain weakness unresolved: SiT achieves only 71.26% F1, acknowledged to require negative reasoning (absence of artifacts as evidence) which the VCR reward doesn't incentivize. Identified but not solved.

Evaluation circularity concern: Reasoning quality assessment uses GPT-4o as judge, which may systematically favor LLM-generated reasoning patterns. Human evaluation is limited (8 subjects, 5 images). Domain expert validation in forensics is absent.

Single-model data bias: All 115k reasoning annotations derive solely from Gemini-2.5 despite using 4 models for feature discovery. Creates potential Gemini-specific perceptual biases. Multi-MLLM distillation acknowledged as future work.

Limited methodological novelty: PRPO is GRPO applied at paragraph level (incremental), VCR/PCR combine existing ideas (CLIP, majority voting, keyword extraction), DF-R5 is a dataset contribution. Overall: strong engineering combining existing techniques rather than fundamental innovation.

High computational overhead inadequately addressed: Test-time PRPO requires 8 H200 GPUs (7.4-13.8 sec latency per batch, Table 20-21). Baseline Gemini-2.5 achieves 80.31% F1 without fine-tuning—unclear if 9.6% gain justifies infrastructure cost.

Incomplete architectural justification: Why LLaVA-7B over alternatives? Why Stage 3 ConvNeXT (10×10 maps)? Reward weight averaging (Eq. 8: equal VCR/PCR weighting) lacks ablation. PCR's binary reward (Eq. 7) may be too sharp.

Dataset transparency gaps: M=7 groups chosen by '85% frequency threshold' without sensitivity analysis; filtering from 150k→115k 'invalid formats with Gemini' is vague (count? criteria?). Limited baseline coverage—no comparison with recent vision-language deepfake methods or learned reward approaches.

strengths: Comprehensive system design combining dataset, architecture, and RL algorithm with strong empirical results (89.91% F1, 4.55/5.0 reasoning quality)
Extensive and thorough ablation studies (Tables 7-11) examining reward components, RL methods, architecture choices, and hyperparameters
Honest error analysis identifying failure modes, particularly the SiT domain limitation (71.26% F1) where near-perfect fakes challenge the artifact-detection paradigm
Clear presentation with informative visualizations (Figure 1) and comprehensive supplementary materials including prompts and implementation details
The DF-R5 dataset with reasoning annotations could be a valuable community resource despite construction limitations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: DX-LLaVA simply replaces ViT with ConvNeXT (known pattern for fine-grained tasks); PRPO is straightforward paragraph-level modification of GRPO without significant algorithmic insight

Critical unexplained result (Table 11): supervised PRPO with ground truth (78.75% F1) severely underperforms unsupervised PRPO (95.88% F1), suggesting fundamental mismatch between intended and actual optimization objectives; explanation about domain-specific overfitting is inadequate and undermines reward design credibility

Severe dependency on Gemini-2.5 throughout: dataset distillation, annotation labels, and implicit training biases; non-reproducible without proprietary API access; missing cross-model generalization experiments (train on Gemini distillation, evaluate with other MLLMs)

Simplistic reward design: VCR uses lossy YAKE keyword extraction + CLIP similarity without learned forensic representations; PCR relies on brittle dictionary matching (e.g., 'no artifacts' incorrectly triggers 'artifacts' key) with simple majority voting ignoring confidence; PCR alone achieves only 70.98% F1, raising questions about why such a weak component is critical

Fundamental unresolved limitation: 71.26% F1 on SiT domain reveals method cannot handle near-perfect fakes requiring negative reasoning; this 28% error rate on advanced generation methods is unacceptable for practical deployment but inadequately addressed

Insufficient justification for paragraph-level granularity: no ablations comparing paragraph vs. token vs. sentence-level advantages; choice appears post-hoc; PRPO vs. GRPO improvement is modest (3.54% on DX-LLaVA in Table 9)

Missing critical implementation details: number of response samples L during test-time inference not clearly stated despite being crucial for cost/performance analysis; fine-tuning computational costs omitted; exact PCR dictionaries only partially specified

Evaluation concerns: quality assessment via GPT-4o introduces another MLLM dependency and potential bias; human evaluation (Appendix D.1) limited to 5 samples per annotator; Gemini-2.5 still achieves 4.20 reasoning score vs. PRPO's 4.55 (not a large gap)

Narrow application scope and reproducibility barriers: face-centric deepfakes only; tested on 5 generative models and static images; dataset construction requires proprietary API access; results vulnerable to model updates

No cross-model generalization: missing critical experiment of training on Gemini-distilled data but evaluating with GPT-4o or Claude to assess transfer; Table 13's low n-gram overlap doesn't prove semantic independence from Gemini's patterns

strengths: Well-motivated technical approach combining DX-LLaVA architecture (ConvNeXT over ViT, justified with detailed analysis) with paragraph-level PRPO algorithm
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: inter-domain generalization testing, comparison with recent MLLMs (Gemini-2.5, GPT-4o), extensive ablations validating each component
Valuable dataset contribution: DF-R5 with 115k reasoning-annotated images addresses real gap in deepfake detection resources
Strong empirical results: 14.65% improvement over SIDA baseline (89.91% F1), reasoning quality 4.55/5.0 exceeding Gemini-2.5 (4.20/5.0), human evaluation validates findings
Novel test-time optimization approach requiring no retraining on new annotated data; unsupervised PRPO outperforming supervised variant is insightful
Honest limitations discussion and impact statement; failure mode analysis reveals fundamental limitations (sparse-artifact detection in SiT domain)
Reproducibility emphasis: detailed prompts, algorithms, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, promised code/dataset release
weaknesses: Reward function design has brittleness: PCR relies on predefined term dictionaries (contents not fully specified) without sensitivity analysis; VCR uses YAKE which isn't validated for forensic relevance

Fundamental limitation acknowledged but unresolved: majority voting in PCR fails when artifact absence indicates fakeness (SiT domain F1=71.26%), suggesting approach struggles with future high-quality fakes
Limited algorithmic novelty: paragraph-level GRPO is incremental; reward functions combine existing techniques (CLIP similarity + term matching) without fundamental innovation
Scope limitations: face-centric only (no body swaps, voice, video); narrow vision encoder/LLM compatibility; dataset heavily reliant on Gemini-2.5 despite bias concerns

Experimental gaps: human evaluation limited to 8 participants on 5 images; stark intra-domain overfitting (99%+ F1) despite generalization focus; computational overhead (7-13 seconds per image) may limit deployment

Key content in appendix: failure analysis (Section E.4) and qualitative examples (Figures 14-16) crucial for understanding but not in main paper; dictionary contents and some implementation details missing
Unvalidated design choices: YAKE keyword extraction for VCR, number of PRPO sampling iterations, how paragraph boundaries determined during inference; generalization to other architectures unexplored
